# last

<link-summary>Takes the last element of an array, or its last n elements in their original order.</link-summary>

<web-summary>last() — Takes the last element of an array, or its last n elements in their original order. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/array</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function last<T>(array: T[]): T | undefined;
function last<T>(array: T[], n: number): T[];
function last<T>(array: T[], n?: number): T | T[] | undefined;
```

This is what `array[array.length - 1]` is written for — an expression that yields `undefined` on an empty array
while looking like it meant something else. `last` says it plainly and returns `undefined` in the same case.

The `n` form takes from the end but preserves the original order: `last([1, 2, 3], 2)` is `[2, 3]`, not `[3, 2]`.
`n` is clamped, so a negative count yields an empty array and a count beyond the length yields the whole array. The
input is not modified.

## Parameters

| Parameter        | Type     | Description                                                          |
| :--------------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `array`          | `T[]`    | The array to read from. Left untouched.                              |
| `n` _(optional)_ | `number` | How many elements to take. An integer; omit it to take a single one. |

## Returns

`T | T[] | undefined` — `T | undefined` when `n` is omitted — the last element, or `undefined` for an empty array. `T[]` when `n` is given — a new array of at most `n` elements, in their original order.

## Throws

| Exception   | Condition                           |
| :---------- | :---------------------------------- |
| `TypeError` | `array` is not an array.            |
| `TypeError` | `n` is given and is not an integer. |

## Examples

### One element, or several

```javascript
last([1, 2, 3]); // => 3
last([]); // => undefined
last([1, 2, 3], 2); // => [2, 3] — order preserved
```

### Reading the most recent entries of a log sheet

<tabs group="code">
<tab title="TypeScript" group-key="ts">
<code-block lang="typescript" src="last.ts" include-symbol="logRecentEntries"/>
</tab>
<tab title="JavaScript" group-key="js">
<code-block lang="javascript">
function logRecentEntries(sheet) {
  const rows = sheet.getDataRange().getValues().slice(1);
  for (const row of last(rows, 10)) {
    Logger.log(row.join(" | "));
  }
}
</code-block>
</tab>
</tabs>

### Clamping

```javascript
last([1, 2], 10); // => [1, 2]
last([1, 2], -1); // => []
last([1, 2], 1.5); // throws TypeError: Input 'n' must be an integer.
```
